chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated from al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from Jamīl ibn Ṣāliḥ, from Abū ʿUbaydah, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a woman who married a man while she already had a husband. He said: “If her first husband is residing with her in the town in which she is, such that she can reach him or he can reach her, then upon her is what is upon the muḥṣan fornicator: stoning. But if her first husband is absent from her, or he is residing with her in the town yet neither can reach the other, then upon her is what is upon the non-muḥṣan adulteress, and there is no liʿān between them.”

I said: Who will stone her and administer the prescribed punishment to her while her husband does not bring her to the Imam and does not want that from her? He said: “The hadd remains Allah’s due upon her body until whoever carries it out does so, and she meets Allah while it is still upon her.”

I said: What if she was ignorant of what she did? He said: “Is she not in Dār al-Hijrah?” I said: Yes. He said: “There is no woman today among the Muslim women except that she knows that it is not halal for a Muslim woman to marry two husbands.”

He said: “And if whenever a woman committed fornication she were to say, ‘I did not know,’ or, ‘I was ignorant that what I did was haram,’ and the hadd were not carried out upon her, then the prescribed punishments would become inoperative.”

key_terms.الرَّجْمَ: stoning as the hadd punishment in the case specified
key_terms.الْحَدَّ: the prescribed legal punishment fixed by the Sacred Law
key_terms.اَلزَّانِيَةِ غَيْرِ الْمُحْصَنَةِ: the adulteress who is not in the state of iḥṣān
key_terms.اَلزَّانِيِ الْمُحْصَنِ: the married adulterer/fornicator who falls under the ruling of iḥṣān
key_terms.دَارِ الْهِجْرَةِ: the land of Islam where such rulings are presumed to be known
key_terms.لِعَانَ: mutual imprecation between spouses in a legal dispute over sexual misconduct

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling in Shiʿi hadith on a woman who marries while she already has a husband?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a woman who marries while still bound to a prior husband, distinguishing between the case of iḥṣān and non-iḥṣān based on the accessibility of the first husband. It also states that the hadd remains due until carried out and rejects a claim of ignorance in a setting where the ruling is considered commonly known.
